newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League regrets U.S. veto of Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: Arab League regrets U.S. veto of Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: The Arab League said on Wednesday the United States veto of a second term for U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali would not bode well for Washington's interests in the Arab world.
"We regret the American position. This position will not serve well the interests of the United States in Arab states," League secretary-general Esmat Abdel Meguid told reporters.

Fourteen of the Security Council's 15 members voted on Tuesday for a new five-year term for Boutros-Ghali but U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright voted against it, saying the U.N. needed someone more amenable to reform.
Washington's veto has sparked Arab and African furore and set Boutros-Ghali's supporters -- a majority in the United Nations -- battling for his return.

The Security Council has agreed to give priority to candidates from Africa on the grounds that if Boutros-Ghali is denied the second term given his predecessors, he should at least be followed by another African.
Prominent League member Egypt also said the U.S. veto was regrettable and President Hosni Mubarak said earlier it was indicative of a "new form of democracy" in the world.
Twenty-one Arab and African countries are members of the Cairo-based Arab League.
